                                 method="AvgPIC",
                                 BurnIn=1000,

                                 p0="p0", p1="p1",
                                 outpath="C:/Users/manawadc/Programs/R_NewHybrids",

                                 method="AvgPIC",
                                 BurnIn=1000,
                                 sweeps=1000,
                                 verbose=3)                            
                                 

            Error in file(file, "rt") : cannot open the connection
            In addition: Warning message:
            In file(file, "rt") :
            cannot open file 'aa-Pofz.csv': No such file or directory


I've checked the function and fount that in one place, "aa-Pofz.csv" has been used instead of "aa-PofZ.csv" with uppercase 'Z' as in other occurrences. . Not sure whether this is the cause for the error massage though.


  if (flag == "bothpar" & plot == TRUE) {
    F1.test <- read.csv(file = "aa-Pofz.csv")
    F1.test <- F1.test[(F1.test$F1 >= pprob), ]
    F1.only <- gl.keep.ind(gl.fixed.used, as.character(F1.test$id),
                           mono.rm = FALSE, verbose = 0)
    mat <- t(as.matrix(F1.only))


I tried to define a new function with  "aa-PofZ.csv", but I could not get it to work. I am not an expert in R coding and I'd be really great full if anyone can help me with this.


Thanks
Chapa

messages.subject: Re: Error in gl.nhybrids function when specified the parental groups.
parts:
Hi Chapa,

I have fixed this bug. You can use this updated function by installing the beta version of dartR, as shown in the code below.

First, download the binary file for your system from:

https://github.com/eriqande/newhybrids/tree/master/bin

Then move the binary file to a folder that is not your R working directory and grant access to the binary, as shown in the code below.

Then try again to run the function.

Cheers,
Luis

library(dartR)
#installing the beta version of dartR
gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "beta")
# grant access to new binary
path_to_nhybrids <- "/your_path/newhybrids"
system(paste0("chmod 755 ",path_to_nhybrids))

test <- platypus.gl
test <- gl.filter.callrate(tets,threshold = 1)

BJ_NHyb <- gl.nhybrids(test,
                       p0=NULL, p1=NULL,
                       outpath=getwd(),
                       nhyb.directory="/nhybrids_folder_path/",
